class.name: PhysXFlowEmitter3D
class.brief_description: A source of smoke, heat and fuel for a [PhysXFlow3D], or a solid in it.
class.description: Feeds the [PhysXFlow3D] its [member flow] path points at; with [member flow] empty it feeds the scene's only [PhysXFlow3D] (a warning asks you to set [member flow] when there are several). So it can live anywhere -- inside a vehicle scene by its wheels, say, following the vehicle -- and a level with several flows sets [member flow] per instance. With [member collision] on, it's a solid instead: the gas inside it takes on its motion and holds nothing. Physics bodies near the gas are solids already (see [member PhysXFlow3D.collide_with_bodies]); this is for shapes that aren't physics bodies.

method.name: get_flow
method.description: The [PhysXFlow3D] this emitter feeds right now, or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_motion_velocity
method.description: This node's world-space velocity over the last physics step (what a solid pushes into the gas).

members.member: Burn amount put in (combustion that is already under way).
Make this a solid the gas flows around, moving with this node, instead of a source.
How strongly the emitter drives the gas toward its values (per second).
Expansion put in: positive pushes gas outward, as from an explosion.
The [PhysXFlow3D] to feed. Empty: the scene's only one.
Fuel put in; it burns above the flow's [member PhysXFlow3D.ignition_temperature], making heat and smoke.
Temperature put in: hot gas rises and glows (see [member PhysXFlow3D.heat_ramp]).
Velocity put in, in this node's own frame (a nozzle turns with the node), in m/s.
